description: The bar chart illustrates the popularity of knowledge associated with correctly and incorrectly answered samples across three domains—Movies, Songs, and Basketball—for three large language models: Llama3 (blue), Qwen2 (red), and ChatGPT (yellow). The vertical axis, labeled “Popularity,” ranges from 0 to 220 with tick marks at intervals of 20. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by domain. Each domain contains six bars grouped by model, representing three types of popularity metrics: “Acc=0 & GT Ans” (incorrectly answered with ground truth answer popularity), “Acc=0 & Gene Ans” (incorrectly answered with generated answer popularity), and “Acc=1 & GT Ans” (correctly answered with ground truth answer popularity), each distinguished by fill pattern (solid, crosshatched, or diagonal lines) as indicated in the legend. In the Movies category, popularity values are generally low, ranging from approximately 20 to 50. In Songs, values increase, with Llama3’s “Acc=0 & GT Ans” reaching ~70 and ChatGPT’s “Acc=1 & GT Ans” at ~75. In Basketball, popularity peaks sharply: Llama3’s “Acc=0 & GT Ans” is ~150, Qwen2’s “Acc=0 & GT Ans” reaches ~185, and ChatGPT’s “Acc=1 & GT Ans” is ~170. Across all domains, the “Acc=0 & GT Ans” bars (incorrect answers with ground truth popularity) tend to be taller than those for “Acc=0 & Gene Ans” (incorrect answers with generated answer popularity), suggesting that ground truth answers in incorrect samples are often more popular than the generated ones. The chart visually emphasizes that popularity is highest in the Basketball domain and that Qwen2 consistently shows the highest popularity values among the models for incorrect samples with ground truth answers.
